exam.title: Art Paper 1 (33/1) - October/November 2023
exam.subject: Art
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: Composition in art refers to
options: the writing down of ones ideas.
the thinking of what one wants to do.
questions.explanation: Composition is how the elements of an artwork are arranged into a whole.

questions.question: Which of the statements below defines the technique of stippling when shading?
options: The use of dots to create value.
The use of lines to create value.
The use of dots in a linear fashion.
Using varying tones to create form.
questions.explanation: Stippling builds up tone and value using small dots rather than lines.

questions.question: Use the images W, X, Y and Z below to answer questions 3 and 4. Which art element has been used effectively in the images above?
questions.explanation: All four images (W, X, Y, Z) are built entirely from lines -- contour lines on the hands, and radiating/zigzag lines in the optical patterns.

questions.question: Which art principle is depicted by image Z?
questions.explanation: The repeated zigzag lines spiralling outward from the centre create a strong sense of rhythm and movement.

questions.question: Which of the images below shows a contemporary art form?
questions.explanation: Image C is a graffiti-style 'HOPE' piece -- street art/graffiti is a contemporary art form, unlike the classical Madonna painting (A), prehistoric rock art (B), or traditional pottery (D).

questions.question: Which set of tools is used in sculpture making?
questions.explanation: Mallets and chisels are the classic carving tools, with pliers useful for wire-based sculpture work.

questions.question: Which painting style was used in the picture below?
questions.explanation: The subject is broken into geometric, overlapping facets shown from multiple angles at once -- the defining feature of Cubism.

questions.question: What is the function of the safety goggles shown below?
options: To prevent bacteria from reaching the user
Protects water from entering a swimmer's eyes
To prevent viruses from entering the painter's eyes
Shields the welder's eyes from hazardous particles
questions.explanation: Flip-lens goggles like these are worn during welding to protect the eyes from sparks, heat and hazardous particles.

questions.question: Which of the following is an emerging health issue?
questions.explanation: Gender Based Violence is widely flagged as an emerging/growing social health issue in Botswana, unlike the other long-established conditions listed.

questions.question: Which famous art master influenced the making of the picture below?
questions.explanation: The swirling sky is drawn in the style of Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night'.

questions.question: Use the information from the table below to answer question 11. Which row shows a wrongly matched art form and art career?
questions.explanation: Row L pairs Painting with 'Weaver' -- weaving is a craft career, not a painting career (a painter would be the correct match).

questions.question: A ceramist makes sculpture with
questions.explanation: A ceramist works with clay, shaping and firing it into pottery or sculpture.

questions.question: Which of the colours listed below are complementary?
questions.explanation: Red and green sit opposite each other on the colour wheel, making them a complementary pair.

questions.question: Use the image below to answer questions 14 and 15. What type of sculpture is shown above?
questions.explanation: The bust combines a classically modelled figure with added wire elements -- different materials and objects combined together is the definition of an assemblage.

questions.question: Which pair of materials below is suitable for making the above sculpture?
questions.explanation: Zinc (for the wire elements) and bee wax (a traditional modelling/casting material for the figure) match the mixed-media look of the piece.

questions.question: Use the image of the artefact below to answer question 16. To which class of artworks does the artefact belong?
questions.explanation: A wire basket like this is a handcrafted item -- it belongs to the craft category of artworks.

questions.question: Use the image of the paper sculpture below to answer question 17. The paper sculpture above is
questions.explanation: The folded, low-poly paper deer head has depth, width and height -- it is a three-dimensional sculpture, not a flat image.

questions.question: What is a mosaic?
options: A flat craft piece put on a window.
An artwork made out of glass to decorate tables.
An artwork that uses various materials to form a composition.
An artwork made by inlaying small pieces of cut material to form a picture.
questions.explanation: A mosaic is built from many small pieces (tile, glass, stone, etc.) inlaid together to form an image.

questions.question: Which of the tools below is suitable for sewing leather pieces together?
questions.explanation: The awl shown at C is the hand tool used to pierce leather and guide thread through it when stitching leather pieces together.

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason for adding sand to clay?
questions.explanation: Sand (grog) opens up the clay body, letting moisture escape more evenly and reducing shrinkage and cracking as it dries and fires.

questions.question: Use the images below showing ornaments X and Y to answer questions 21 to 23. What type of ornament is X?
questions.explanation: A beaded necklace like X is a piece of jewellery, worn on the body as a personal ornament.

questions.question: Which material was used to make ornament X?
questions.explanation: Ornament X is a multi-strand necklace made of threaded beads.

questions.question: Which art principle is shown in ornament Y?
questions.explanation: Ornament Y's decoration is built from a diamond motif repeated across the piece -- repetition of a motif is the definition of pattern.

questions.question: An artwork painted on a wall surface is called a
questions.explanation: A mural is a work of art painted directly onto a wall or ceiling.

questions.question: Which of the following terms is defined as the art of a beautiful handwriting?
questions.explanation: Calligraphy is the art of decorative, stylised handwriting or lettering.

questions.question: Use the images K and L below to answer questions 26 and 27. What is the function of the cultural mask K?
options: It is used as disguise at night.
It is worn when celebrating a specific event.
It is used to scare kids during a traditional wedding.
questions.explanation: Cultural/ceremonial masks like K are traditionally worn as part of marking or celebrating a specific cultural event.

questions.question: Where can the mask L be used?
questions.explanation: The ornate, decorative style of mask L is typical of masquerade masks worn at carnivals.

questions.question: What are the functions of the cards shown below?
options: To invite people to a birthday party
To wish a sick person good health
questions.explanation: Both cards use hearts and Valentine's Day imagery, which are used to celebrate love and life.

questions.question: Which of the following is an awareness poster?
questions.explanation: Poster B ('STOP BULLYING') is designed to raise awareness of a social issue, unlike the artistic image (A), the motivational quote card (C), or the tourism poster (D).

questions.question: Which principle of design was applied in the card below?
questions.explanation: The stars and dots are arranged evenly around the centred '2022' text, giving the card a radially balanced design.

questions.question: What is a logo?
options: Free form images that are found in posters.
An identification symbol used by companies.
questions.explanation: A logo is a graphic mark or symbol that identifies a company or organisation.

questions.question: Which of the art elements below is commonly repeated when decorating fabrics?
questions.explanation: Fabric decoration typically repeats a motif's shape across the surface to build a pattern.

questions.question: What is a glaze?
options: A natural colour of fired clay.
A chemical used to coat food.
A chemical that tints glass panes.
A substance used to give pottery a decorative colour.
questions.explanation: Glaze is a glass-forming coating applied to pottery before firing to give it colour, shine and a sealed surface.

questions.question: Which of the machines below is used for weaving?
questions.explanation: The machine at B is a weaving loom, with its frame, shuttle and foot pedals for interlacing threads; A is a printing press, C a potter's wheel, and D a sewing machine.

questions.question: Which of the following is a visual art related career?
questions.explanation: Wood carving is a visual/sculptural art career; the other options are not visual art fields.

questions.question: Which of the tools below is commonly used by photographers?
questions.explanation: The camera is the essential tool a photographer uses to capture an image.

questions.question: Which of the images below shows a relief sculpture?
questions.explanation: Image B is a classical stone frieze where the figures are carved so they project from a flat background -- the definition of relief sculpture.

questions.question: Which of the following are properties of clay?
questions.explanation: Porosity and plasticity are physical properties of clay itself; the other options are techniques used to work it, not properties of the material.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a property of wallpaper?
options: It is a permanent wall decoration.
It is used to protect and decorate walls.
questions.explanation: Wallpaper can be removed or replaced, so it is not a permanent wall decoration -- unlike the other statements, which are true of wallpaper.

questions.question: Which print making techniques may have been used in the picture below?
questions.explanation: The fine, dense parallel linework of the flamingo print is typical of combined wood cut and etching techniques.
